articles.title: At least 30 people killed in high-speed train collision in central Spain
articles.summary: By Emma Pinedo and Victoria Waldersee MADRID, Oct 28 (Reuters) - At least 30 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said. Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha television showed a derailed train with several carriages remaining on an elevated ‌section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line. Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of ‌the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident. "We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train," he said. A person ​briefed on the disaster said an express operated by Spanish train operator Iryo stopped near Toledo due to a signal fault, on orders from infrastructure manager ADIF, when it was struck by another high-speed train on. A train operated by Renfe then struck the stationary train at high speed, causing several carriages of both trains to derail, the person said. There was no immediate response to a Reuters request for comment from Iryo or Renfe. PASSENGER DESCRIBES SEEING FATALITIES Castilla-La Mancha regional government said the death toll had risen to 30 from 10 after earlier warning it could rise. Jesús Pérez Martín, mayor of the nearby town of Los Yébenes, said the situation was "horrific" and pointed to a severe tragedy. "They are telling me about mutilations ‌and very serious injuries," he told RTVE. Health Minister Mónica García urged people in ⁠a post on X  to donate blood. Eduarda, a passenger on the Iryo train, told Cadena SER radio she felt a strong impact that threw her forward, initially making her think the train had made an emergency stop. She only realised the seriousness of the accident after seeing injured people and being told to evacuate. After climbing down an embankment to safety, ⁠she saw what she described as a catastrophic scene, with part of the train hanging down the slope and a fire in one carriage. Emergency responders, including a helicopter, police and ambulances, arrived within about 20 minutes, she said. "I saw dead people," she said. SECOND FATAL ACCIDENT ON LINE IN A YEAR Castilla-La Mancha region spokesperson Esther Padilla said 147 people had been travelling on the Iryo train and 397 on the Renfe train. The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to ​the ​same operators on the same line that killed 46 people. That crash in January, which occurred after a train derailed and smashed ​into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province, triggered a debate about the level ‌of investment in railway maintenance in recent years. ELECTION DUE NEXT MONTH The Renfe and Iryo trains crashed just after 9 a.m. (0800 GMT), causing two Iryo wagons to derail, a spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha region said, adding that the cause was not yet clear. Renfe said it had activated a special line for families of victims and expressed its condolences. Iryo said it had activated emergency protocols. The latest accident comes as Spain gears up for an election on November 29. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's agenda, published on the Spanish government's website, had been cleared for the day. The opposition People's Party also cancelled all campaign events, a spokesperson said. "Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families," Sanchez said on X. Manuel Galan, the mayor of the nearby town of Urda, told Cadena SER that emergency services had asked the town council to prepare ‌emergency facilities, including a sports hall, to accommodate passengers and the injured. RAIL SAFETY RECORD Accidents, including derailments and collisions, increased from 45 ​in 2016 to 57 in 2024 and 69 last year, according to Spain's railway safety authority. In the same period, problems such ​as deterioration and breaks in the rails went from 494 and 667, a level below the 716 ​registered in 2024. Some 25 million passengers used a high-speed train in Spain in the first half of the year, a decline of roughly 14% compared with the same period ‌last year, according to a Reuters analysis of data from Spain's competition authority. European Commission data ​shows Spain's maintenance investment in its roughly 4,000 km (2,485 ​miles) of high-speed lines has lagged large European peers, despite an unmatched drive to expand the network. Spain spent an average of about €1.5 billion a year from 2018 to 2022 on its high-speed network, more than any other country. However, the vast majority went to new infrastructure with only some 16% earmarked for maintenance, renewal and upgrades. Spain had registered among the lowest fatality rates in the EU from train incidents ​before this year's accidents, with just one or fewer fatalities per thousand kilometres ‌of railway tracks, according to the latest available Eurostat data from 2024. Over 90% of Spain's train network is equipped with the highest level of safety control systems in the European Union, according ​to the EU railway agency. Alongside Belgium and Switzerland, its networks have the largest amount of rail equipped with a Europe-wide signalling standard. (Reporting by David Latona, Emma Pinedo, Mireia Merino, Corina ​Pons, Victoria Waldersee, Benjamin Mejias and Joan Faus; Writing by Charlie Devereux; Editing by Toby Chopra and Alison Williams) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/two-high-speed-trains-rear-083828936.html

articles.title: Classified material missing from Epstein files, documents suggest
articles.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche has long maintained that the so-called Epstein files, even those kept from the public, contain no secret information related to national security. When the document releases began last winter, Blanche noted that the Epstein Files Transparency Act authorized withholding information in the interest of national security or foreign policy, but said, "no files are being withheld or redacted on that basis." "There's not some tranche of super-secret documents about Jeffrey Epstein that we're withholding, we're actually not withholding anything based upon [national defense information]," said Blanche, who was deputy attorney general at the time. But the contents of at least three documents in the massive tranche of files indicate classified information was included in files collected by the DOJ. One of the documents shows Blanche's Office of the Deputy Attorney General itself received classified material related to Epstein in March 2025. By law, material can only be classified for national security purposes. What exactly was classified and why remains a mystery. The Department of Justice says it collected 6 million pages of material and ultimately released over 3 million of those pages after reviewing for duplication, attorney-client privilege and relevance to Jeffrey Epstein. Congressional challenges and a lawsuit are casting doubts on the DOJ's claims and demanding the release of more documents that were held back. Clues about classified material Included among the Epstein files is an eight-page timeline of the FBI's New York office's initial efforts last year to track down and deliver its voluminous files to the Justice Department's Washington headquarters. On March 25, 2025, one document shows delivery of "16 Epstein items to ODAG," referring to the Office of the Deputy Attorney General. Among them, items No. 2 and No. 6 are described as "Epstein Transparency Project - Classified Material" and "CDs with classified materials (x2)." The Epstein Transparency Project refers to the Justice Department's effort to review the files and redact , withhold or clear them for release. It is not clear what exactly was identified as classified. Each CD was likely capable of holding hundreds of megabytes of material. Also in the files is an email sent that same day from the unit chief of the National Security Classification Operations Unit — an office whose role is to review FBI documents for classification or declassification. The email includes an attachment labeled "Epstein - Classified Document Memo.docx." The body of the email says there were three documents "identified that remain classified." One was described as an "FBI document which is classified when see-through." A redaction obscures the unit chief's description of the other two documents. The identity of the email's recipient is also redacted. It's also not clear whether the two documents — the email and the list — are referring to the same classified material. Coding system reveals missing pages A CBS News analysis of a numerical coding system used by the DOJ to organize the Epstein files offers clues about some of the documents the department has withheld. The codes don't reveal what's missing, but they do show where gaps exist, raising questions about the DOJ's explanation for why documents were withheld. Among the missing documents are pages from Epstein's own financial records collected as evidence in a federal prosecution. Here's how it works: Documents from the Epstein files are labeled with a string of numbers beginning with the letters EFTA stamped on the bottom right-hand corner; EFTA stands for Epstein Files Transparency Act. Those are called Bates numbers — a common way of organizing massive document batches in legal cases. Every page receives its own number. In the Epstein files, the sequence goes from 1 to 2,858,498, which is the tally of approximately how many pages of documents were released. According to the DOJ, other documents — including court records and investigative files they've previously released — bring the total to over 3 million. Alongside the Epstein files' Bates numbers are other, older coding numbers that appear on many documents. This indicates that those documents had previously been used in federal legal cases, potentially collected as part of an earlier subpoena. For instance, Bates coding on some of the documents is from the Ghislaine Maxwell criminal case and was used to organize files given to Maxwell's legal team ahead of her 2021 trial as part of the discovery process. Other Bates numbers indicate documents were collected from Epstein's banks, including JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank, during the FBI's investigation into his trafficking activities. Similar gap analyses have been done in the past by independent researchers. Missing financial documents Finding gaps in these documents is a simple process of counting. In tens of thousands of instances, the main EFTA number will advance by one but the other Bates numbers advance by two or more. Those gaps indicate pages that had been there before were likely removed at some point after the DOJ obtained them. Take the images below: The EFTA number advances by one but the JPM-SDNY and SDNY_GM numbers advance by 2, as do the page numbers from the original document. In another example, a series of around 4,500 images of checks from Epstein's accounts has gaps where 66 of those check images should be. Oftentimes the missing image is only the front or the back of the check, although in several cases both are missing. Comparing all of these numbers against the final EFTA page numbers, it is possible to calculate that there are tens of thousands of pages of documents that are missing from these sections, with no clear reason why. "Financial records were not a permissible category for removal," Barbara McQuade, the former U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Michigan, told CBS News. Like every federal prosecutor, she says she is very familiar with Bates numbers. "It's the reason you have Bates numbers, so you notice something like that," she said. The DOJ hasn't responded to CBS News' recent inquiries about the Epstein files, but it has previously said that every document required to be released by the Epstein Files Transparency Act has been released, and the remaining files were unrelated, privileged, or were duplicative. Email gaps Another sequence of Bates numbers that provide a map to where documents were removed appears to be from a preliminary processing of the files. One large sequence of those have "R1" in between EFTA and the page number. This R1 numbering is found across approximately 995,000 released pages, between p. 61 and p. 2,214,171 in the files. Each page is also labeled with an EFTA page number. While the EFTAs are sequential, the R1s have gaps which range from 1 page to hundreds of pages. Each time a gap appears — for example, if the EFTA advances by 1 but the R1 advances by 2 — it's evidence that pages were removed. By comparing these sequences it's possible to identify gaps where documents, mostly emails, were removed between that earlier review and the final release. No partial emails turned up in the thousands of documents we examined, so the removals appear to be entire email exchanges. Here's what a section of that looks like: The emails are not sequential in date and jump by days, months and years, so knowing what was removed from context is simply not possible. But the results of calculating the differences between the first and last of the numbers in this earlier sequence versus the later sequence is 1.2 million pages, which is the total number of identified gaps from just this one section. Most of the documents in this section are emails to or from Jeffrey Epstein, including communication with young women who would later accuse him of abuse; email exchanges with his business associates; messages to or from his assistant, Lesley Groff; or emails sent or received by Ghislaine Maxwell. "De-duping" There is one possible explanation for many of the email gaps. Instructions given to DOJ attorneys working on processing the redactions state: "If the document is an email chain and the most-inclusive email (i.e., containing all the back-and-forth) has already been reviewed and redacted as appropriate for production, the interstitial back-and-forth can be marked as duplicates." In other words, all emails exchanged prior to the last email in a chain can be considered a duplicate, because the last one should include all of the messages, and eliminating the duplicates will speed up the redaction process. Once a document is marked as a duplicate, it would likely be excluded from the files. If that was the case, this was only partially accomplished because duplicate emails still exist throughout the files. There's also the possibility that errors in the process could have resulted in crucial emails mistakenly being deleted. Lack of transparency The review and redaction process was conducted by hundreds of DOJ attorneys working under a compressed timeline. Given the scale of the task, it's possible that pages were withheld as a result of honest mistakes. But without a roadmap to the redactions and removals, it's impossible to make that determination. Independent journalist Katie Phang is suing the Justice Department, seeking the release of more files as well as an explanation of redactions and removals. A federal judge has made several rulings in her favor and the DOJ is appealing those rulings. As part of her lawsuit, Phang is asking the court to appoint a special master to review the files. "If it wasn't intentional, then was it gross negligence? Were you just lazy? If it was intentional then I think there's [expletive] there that they don't want people to see," Phang told CBS News. "My speculation runs an entire spectrum of reaction — but at the end of the day it just makes the DOJ look bad." The DOJ has acknowledged making several mistakes. It admitted to removing, and then restoring, a photo of now Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on a 2012 visit to Epstein's island , contradicting claims Lutnick had previously made about his contacts with Epstein . Last year, DOJ officials claimed a minute was missing from prison security video from the night Epstein died, which turned out to not be true . "This is a case where the process has inhibited public trust in what is ultimately released, and there's a long tradition of this, whether it's the Pentagon Papers or the Epstein files," said attorney Stanley Brand, a veteran litigator and distinguished fellow in law and government at Penn State Dickinson Law. "This is just another piece where the government process, where making this stuff available just fuels suspicion that there's something we're not seeing, and I don't know that ever gets resolved." articles.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu remains far from defeated
articles.summary: JERUSALEM (AP) — Anxious Israelis watched election results take shape Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him. Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it’s not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in the next parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel. Netanyahu seeks to remain the country's longest-serving prime minister. In defiant comments after the vote, he dismissed the idea of partnering with Arab parties — whose constituents make up 20% of Israel’s population — as treasonous. “We must establish a strong, right-wing, nationalist government,” Netanyahu said. “We must not endanger Israel and establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties.” His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot , has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group. But it remains to be seen whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office. With 77% of votes counted, Netanyahu’s Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.4%. The count from Israel’s Central Elections Committee does not indicate how many seats each will have in parliament, the 120-seat Knesset. Likud's share in the previous election in 2022 was 23.4%. Netanyahu faces a setback but not outright defeat Nearly 78% of eligible voters turned out, the highest since 1999. Final results are expected in the coming days, including from hundreds of thousands of absentee ballots yet to be counted from military personnel and diplomats. Voting reflected unease over Netanyahu's alliance with the far-right and anger in a war-weary nation over military draft exemptions for the significant ultra-Orthodox Jewish population . But results suggest opponents were unable to capitalize on the grief caused by the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack to decisively push him from office. One partner losing support, however, was far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir . For many Israelis, he represented the worst strain of Netanyahu’s government, openly taunting Palestinian detainees and asserting that many in Gaza are “not even people.” Exit polls by major Israeli TV stations Tuesday night suggested Netanyahu’s governing coalition shrank. Vote-counting suggested Likud would remain the largest party and best placed to be tapped to form a government by Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog. The president, however, isn't required to task the leader of the party holding the most seats. “I prefer that (Netanyahu) assembles the coalition,” said Ran Cohen, a Jerusalem resident. “He’s the only one who knows how to do the job properly, knows how to speak to the world.” The most obvious path to a parliamentary majority could involve Eisenkot partnering with Arab-led parties, but that's politically challenging. In a speech early Wednesday that focused on national unity, Eisenkot pledged to form a government and promised “a new era — an era of hope." If no one can put together a majority coalition, new elections could be held early next year. Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate. Whether thousands of Israelis living abroad would again fly back home to vote , and whether Arab voters would again surge to the polls, is unclear. Arab-led parties could hold the key Confronted with Arab parties’ strong election showing, Israelis have renewed a debate about identity. “We have no future here if we do not stop being afraid," said Yair Golan, whose Democrats party supports bringing Arab-led parties into a coalition. "We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes.” Israel’s Arab citizens are descendants of Palestinians who remained in the state after its creation in 1948. They often face discrimination and are viewed with wariness because of their solidarity with the Palestinian cause. That suspicion intensified after Oct. 7, even though Arab citizens were also among those killed and abducted . Netanyahu had warned that Arab parties could make or break the election. He won’t work with the Arab-led parties, and they have also ruled that out. The mood was joyful overnight at the headquarters of the United Arab List, the lone Arab party to ever join a governing coalition, briefly, in 2021. “We are here, we are not on the sidelines,” party leader Mansour Abbas declared. Some Israelis found that an unusual, if not uncomfortable, prospect. “We are little by little coming to a situation where we have to face reality," said Hanna Doukhan, a voter in Tel Aviv. "I don’t see a possibility to form a government without the Arabs.” “We don’t want the government with the Arab people,” said Michal Shiloh in Jerusalem, reflecting a rightward shift among some younger Israelis. Others were hopeful. “This would open the door to repairing our society" while preserving Israel as the national home of the Jewish people, said Eti Wissotzky-Cohen in Tel Aviv. Minority governments also are possible, but they must rely on cooperation from parties outside the government to pass legislation. Attitudes over Netanyahu will shape the days ahead Netanyahu has had a nearly unbroken 17-year rule. Israelis were divided over him even before the deadliest attack in the country’s history. The resulting wars , along with settler violence in the occupied West Bank, have stoked worldwide outrage , straining ties with Israel’s closest allies and fueling a rise in antisemitism. Netanyahu’s supporters believe he is protecting Israel’s security and Jewish identity in the face of international pressure and liberal elites at home. Detractors say Netanyahu, facing an ongoing corruption trial , dragged out the war in Gaza and its hostage crisis for political reasons. They say he is undermining Israel’s independent judiciary. And they accuse his government of allowing ultra-Orthodox religious Jews to avoid military conscription . Eisenkot is viewed by supporters as a capable leader with sterling security credentials. His son and two nephews were killed in Gaza, and his backers believe that he feels deeply the country's pain. Parties that likely would partner with him have vowed to improve Israel’s international standing and work to conscript ultra-Orthodox men while bolstering the independence of the judiciary. ___ Mednick reported from Tel Aviv, Israel. Associated Press writers across Israel contributed to this report. articles.title: Judge appears skeptical of Trump's push to set aside 20,000 California ballots
articles.summary: The federal district judge overseeing the Justice Department's lawsuit asking California to segregate roughly 20,000 ballot belonging to individuals it claims are "likely" noncitizens appeared skeptical of the DOJ's efforts to seek emergency action just a week from the state's election. U.S. District Judge David O. Carter said in court Tuesday he intends to appoint a special master to probe DOJ's process that led it to compile the list of alleged 20,000 likely non-citizens, dealing a setback to the Trump administration's attempt to quickly intervene in the election. Judge Carter did not rule by the conclusion of the hearing on the DOJ request for a temporary restraining order against the state, though he appeared skeptical of the department's late-stage attempt to force what he described as a "monumental change" in California's ongoing administration of its election. Daniel Cole/Reuters - PHOTO: California election fraud hearing DOJ sues California over alleged non-citizens on voter rolls Carter told the parties he intends to issue some kind of ruling governing proceedings on the case moving forward by tomorrow. Bill Essayli, a controversial Trump-installed leader of the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Central District of California, argued in the hearing that the administration was simply pushing for the state to be in compliance with federal law barring non-citizens from casting votes. But state officials and other legal advocates opposing the DOJ lawsuit countered that the litigation violated longstanding Constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections -- and could have chaotic consequences for the state in tabulating final vote counts in the weeks ahead. Appeals court declines to step in on Trump administration's California voting case Notably in closing out the hearing, Judge Carter appeared to admonish the administration over its recent letters to state officials around California suggesting it could prosecute them if they are involved in tabulating ballots that could be from the list of alleged likely noncitizens. "This court believes it would be wise that any threats to state and county elected employees cease immediately," Carter said. "Good night." 'High percentage' of DOJ's California noncitizen voters list born in US, preliminary LA County analysis shows On Monday, a federal appeals court rejected a request from the DOJ to issue an order requiring California to set aside the 20,000 ballots from its list, kicking the back to the district court. Earlier this month, the DOJ filed suit against California , accusing the state of failing to review the list of alleged noncitizens that the Trump administration claimed were sent mail-in ballots for next week's midterm election. In court papers filed earlier last week, Los Angeles officials said a preliminary analysis of 200 of the names on the 20,000-person list, included a "high percentage" of individuals who say they were born in the U.S. and many more who have no voting history at all. articles.title: Trump and Talarico draw competing crowds in an unlikely Texas battleground
articles.summary: President Trump and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) shared their competing visions Tuesday as the two held dueling rallies in the Lone Star State one week before the midterm elections. Trump did two rallies in Texas — the first in Corpus Christi and another in Lubbock . It’s his fourth trip to Texas to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Talarico held his own rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. He was in Corpus Christi on Saturday. The Texas race is one of the most contested and watched Senate races in the country. Talarico and Paxton remain close in the polls — Real Clear Polling calls the race a toss-up, with Talarico holding a slight lead. A Democrat winning the Senate seat would be a shock — none have won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988, and Trump won the state by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Democrats are vying to take control of the House and the Senate. The party would need to win four seats to win control of the Senate. The president started off his rally in Corpus Christi saying that Texans would defeat “Democrat Communist James Talafreako,” using the nickname he’s given to the candidate. At both rallies, Trump criticized Talarico on a range of issues like immigration, the Second Amendment and barbecue. “If you’re running in Texas and if you don’t like guns, and if you don’t like meat and if you don’t like oil, I think you should be losing by a lot,” Trump said at the first rally about Talarico. “Where the hell did they get this guy?” Trump spoke heavily about the Venezuelan oil tanker that arrived in Texas on Tuesday that is carrying oil to be refined in the state. He said that Talarico would try to take it away. “Talafreako stated that he wants to dismantle Texas oil and gas and capitalism itself. He wants to take it apart,” Trump continued, adding that Talarico will “kill millions of Texas jobs.” In Lubbock, Trump said Talarico “wants to get rid of your guns. He wants to get rid of your oil. Wants to get rid of your meat. He can't stand the stuff.” Talarico has denied being vegan and said he supports the Second Amendment, but advocates for gun control. Talarico, for his part, thanked Texans for showing up for his rally in Lubbock, just three miles away from Trump’s, invoking Trump’s nickname for him. “That’s a lot of Talafreakos in one room,” he said. He said Texans are “ready for change” and hit the Trump administration over the Iran war and tariffs. “Change that will roll back these corrupt tariffs that are raising grocery prices. Change that will end this corrupt war in the Middle East, driving up gas prices,” he said. “We are done with the extremism and the corruption. We're done with the politics of division, and we are ready for something new.” The Democratic Texan hit on Paxton, calling him the “most corrupt politician in Texas.” “Ken Paxton is everything that's wrong with our politics,” he said. “He doesn't serve us. articles.title: Judge rules a top federal prosecutor is 'unlawfully serving' and bars him from cases
articles.summary: First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli in June 2025. (Damian Dovarganes / Associated Press) A federal judge on Tuesday  ruled that Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as Los Angeles’ top federal prosecutor and ordered him disqualified from overseeing two criminal cases, rejecting the Justice Department’s latest effort to preserve his authority. Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright, however, delayed the disqualifications from taking effect while he considers an anticipated government request for a stay pending appeal. Although the order applies to two prosecutions, Seabright rejected the legal arrangement that has allowed Essayli to continue leading the office under the title of first assistant U.S. attorney. He concluded that the Justice Department had unlawfully delegated powers so sweeping that Essayli in effect occupied the U.S. attorney’s position. “In sum, Essayli is unlawfully serving as a ‘de facto’ United States Attorney,” Seabright wrote. After learning about Seabright’s ruling from The Times, Essayli on Tuesday afternoon said that his office expected it and that the case “will be decided by the Supreme Court.” In a follow-up email, he said, “I look forward to serving in my current role until then.” H. Dean Steward, a defense attorney who filed a renewed motion in August challenging Essayli’s authority, called the decision “a victory for the rule of law and the U.S. Constitution.” “The Trump administration ignored the laws governing the appointment of U.S. Attorneys and got caught in Los Angeles,” he said in an emailed statement. “Trump and his Department of Justice violated the law again and again in an effort to install minions as chief federal prosecutors.” The dispute is part of a nationwide battle over the Trump administration’s efforts to install its chosen prosecutors without Senate confirmation. Alina Habba stepped down as New Jersey’s top federal prosecutor in December after an appeals court found her appointment unlawful. In Virginia, a judge’s finding that Lindsey Halligan was unlawfully appointed led to the dismissal of indictments against former FBI Director James Comey and New York Atty. Gen. Letitia James. In his Tuesday ruling, Seabright declined to dismiss the indictments against defendants in the two cases that he banned Essayli from overseeing. Jaime Hector Ramirez and Tu Anh Tran had not shown the substantial prejudice required for that relief, he said in response to attorneys’ requests to dismiss the indictments. His order bars Essayli from participating in or supervising their cases, including overseeing the attorneys handling them. Seabright last year ruled that Essayli was “not lawfully serving” as acting U.S. attorney in Los Angeles, but allowed him to continue exercising authority as a special attorney and first assistant U.S. attorney. The new decision follows a U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals ruling rejecting a similar arrangement for Nevada prosecutor Sigal Chattah. The appellate court ruled that the Department of Justice cannot keep an official who has not been confirmed by the Senate in charge of a U.S. attorney’s office simply by giving that person a different title and the full powers of the job. The Trump administration has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to review the Nevada decision, arguing that federal law allows the attorney general to delegate a vacant office’s powers and install a new first assistant as its acting leader. The Supreme Court has not said whether it will take up the case. The Justice Department sought to address the 9th Circuit ruling through a revised delegation of authority expressly excluding certain powers reserved for a U.S. attorney. At an Oct. 13 hearing, Assistant U.S. Atty. Alexander Robbins argued before Seabright that the revised delegation placed Essayli’s authority on the permissible side of the line drawn by the appeals court. Seabright found that the revision made no meaningful difference because those powers could not have been delegated to Essayli in the first place. “Withholding the three specific statutory powers mentioned in the revised designation order in reality withholds nothing,” Seabright wrote. A former Republican member of the California Assembly from Riverside, Essayli has used his position to act as one of Trump’s fiercest legal foot soldiers. He has pursued criminal charges against protesters, activists and immigrants while dropping cases involving administration allies and supporting lawsuits challenging transgender and environmental policies in California. Essayli was sworn in as interim U.S. attorney in April 2025. Around the time he hit that role’s 120-day limit, he resigned and then-Atty. Gen. Pam Bondi appointed him as a special attorney and designated him first assistant in an attempt to make him acting U.S. attorney. Seabright rejected that maneuver last year. But the judge initially permitted him to supervise prosecutions in his other roles — an arrangement the subsequent 9th Circuit ruling undermined. Trump still had not nominated anyone to serve as U.S. attorney for the Central District of California as of Tuesday’s ruling, Seabright noted. At the Oct. 13 hearing, Robbins said the government would appeal any disqualification ruling and warned of “the chaotic practical effects” of an order taking effect without a stay. Under the schedule accepted by Seabright, prosecutors have five business days after the ruling to seek a stay pending appeal. If he denies that request, the disqualifications would take effect one week later, subject to further orders from him or an appellate court. articles.title: Federal prosecutors fail to get grand jury indictment against Cassidy Hutchinson
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors were rebuffed in their effort to secure an indictment against former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her testimony related to the Jan. 6, 2021, assault on the U.S. Capitol, according to four sources briefed on the grand jury proceedings. The Justice Department has not yet responded to a request for comment. The Washington Post first reported that the grand jury declined to indict Hutchinson. The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division has been handling the Hutchinson investigation, CBS News previously reported, and during a hearing on another matter Tuesday, a litigator with the division, Neville Hedley, told U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui that the grand jury had not concurred on the proposed indictment. Hedley did not say who the defendant was, but multiple sources confirmed it was Hutchinson. Hutchinson, who was a top aide to White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, angered President Trump's allies and his base when she testified in 2022 before the House select committee investigating the 2021 Capitol attack. In depositions and congressional testimony, Hutchinson said that Mr. Trump and Meadows were warned on Jan. 6 that some of his supporters were carrying weapons to the Capitol, but Mr. Trump said he didn't care — and he tried to order officials to remove the magnetometers at the rally where he spoke that morning. She also relayed a story she said had been told to her by then-White House deputy chief of staff Tony Ornato, in which Mr. Trump grew incensed after his lead Secret Service agent would not drive him to the Capitol after the president's speech to supporters. During that address on the White House Ellipse, he had encouraged them to go to the Capitol, where Congress was confirming the Electoral College results from the 2020 election. He told supporters that "after this, we're going to walk down, and I'll be there with you." Hutchinson testified that Ornato had told her that in the car, Mr. Trump lunged at the steering wheel. Her account was later contradicted by Mr. Trump's driver, who in sworn testimony claimed that the president never tried to grab the steering wheel. CBS News could not determine precisely which parts of Hutchinson's testimony were being scrutinized by prosecutors. According to media reports, House Republican allies of the president made the referral to the Justice Department. articles.title: Judge tosses new charges against ex-FBI officials in Hunter Biden case and criticizes DOJ
articles.summary: Oct. 27 (UPI) -- A federal judge on Tuesday tossed new obstruction charges the Justice Department filed against two former FBI agents accused of lying to Congress about an investigation into Hunter Biden. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia expressed anger at the federal prosecutors who filed the superseding complaint shortly after midnight Tuesday, CBS News reported. The complaints were unsworn and unsigned. "We have never had complaints filed that are unsigned," Faruqui said. "It is inappropriate. It harms the defendants. "I am frustrated that I got it in the middle of the night. But I am much more concerned that it is filed on the public record." Former agents Nikki Flores, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, surrendered on arrest warrants Friday that charged them with lying to Congress about their involvement in the Foreign Influence Task Force investigating the Biden family during the 2020 election cycle. They each faced one count of making a false statement. The charges were announced by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro. "Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system, but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it's time to bring the hammer of justice down on them," Pirro said in a statement on X . "When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation's security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold." Prosecutors filed the new complaint to the public court docket Tuesday, adding new charges of obstruction and attempted obstruction of a congressional proceeding. Faruqui said the complaint was never reviewed by him to determine if there was probable cause a crime was committed. He said filing a complaint without judicial review was unprecedented and caused him to question the Justice Department's motivations. The magistrate ordered the complaint to be struck from the record and said the Justice Department could try filing new charges using standard procedures. "Everything you're doing is making me more and more concerned," Faruqui told federal prosecutors. "Why today on this one case have you changed the entire history of how you charge cases? It makes it look like the United States is afraid of me trying to find probable cause." Federal prosecutor John Borchert said it was the first time he'd been aware of a criminal complaint being filed in this manner, as well. He said, though, that prosecutors "are not afraid of a probable cause finding." In a court hearing Tuesday, a lawyer for Flores expressed outrage on behalf of the defense team about the unsigned criminal count added hours before the hearing. "The evidence is mounting that this prosecution is about some political football and not the law or the facts in this case," attorney Mary Dohrmann said in court. "What is going on at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office? In the middle of the night, the government filed an unsigned and unsworn complaint attempting to fix the issues with their original charge against Ms. Flores and adding a new charge just as meritless as the first one" the defense team said in a statement, according to CNBC . "In our combined decades of DOJ service, we have never seen or even heard of something like this being filed. That's because the public lodging of criminal charges must be authorized by the grand jury, a judge, or the defendant herself. "Here, the government has taken that power for itself in a desperate attempt to delay our client's right to challenge the charges in court and litigate this case in the media, rather than the courtroom." articles.title: Utah authorities connect serial killer Ted Bundy to another 1970s homicide
articles.summary: DNA connects serial killer Ted Bundy to the death of another Utah teenager, authorities announced Tuesday, exactly 52 years after her body was discovered in the woods by a hunter. Bundy has been dead since 1989, but the tally of his confirmed victims continues to grow due to advances in DNA testing. He killed at least 30 women and girls in multiple states in the 1970s, and many more escaped or survived with injuries. Investigators are satisfied that Bundy was responsible for killing 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith in 1974, a death that had long been listed as a cold case, Summit County Attorney Margaret Olson said at a news conference. They were able to close the case by making crucial connections with DNA found on Smith and Laura Aime, another Bundy victim whose case was resolved last April in Utah County. Bundy's DNA was on file in Florida, where he was convicted and ultimately executed. Besides that evidence, Smith’s death showed hallmarks of Bundy’s “pattern, motive, means and opportunity,” Olson said. Decades-old evidence was key to the case Utah's state crime lab got new technology in 2023 that extracts DNA from samples even if they are small, degraded from age or contain DNA from multiple people. “This case demonstrates the importance of preserving evidence,” said Salt Lake County Sheriff Rosie Rivera, whose department has also investigated homicides linked to Bundy. “We have to solve these cases to the best of our ability,” she said, explaining the importance of tapping science, even so many years later. "Nobody is just going to walk away and just blame everything on Ted Bundy, even though many cases have been that way. Here in the state of Utah, we take it very seriously.” Smith's relatives were contacted about the findings but declined to attend the news conference and declined to speak to reporters, the Summit County Sheriff's Office said. Her parents are deceased. Smith's father was police chief in Midvale, south of Salt Lake City. She was at a pizza parlor and a restaurant before she disappeared on Oct. 18, 1974, The Salt Lake Tribune reported at the time. Nine days later, her body was found in Summit County. “With every case closure, may we stomp the memory of Ted Bundy out,” Utah County Sgt. Mike Reynolds said. Bundy investigations are not finished Bundy was executed by electric chair in Florida in 1989 after being convicted of three murders, including the killing of two women at the Chi Omega sorority house at Florida State University. He gave a series of confessions in his final days, including to some crimes that were previously unknown to police. Not all of those cases have been confirmed. Besides Florida and Utah, authorities said Bundy had victims in Colorado, Idaho and Washington state. They said they're especially working to solve the 1974 death of 16-year-old Nancy Wilcox of Utah. Solving the Smith homicide “does not close the book on Ted Bundy,” said Det. Ben Pender of the Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office, which has the Wilcox investigation. “Information kind of leads to Ted Bundy but again we're not for certain on Nancy Wilcox. We're going to continue to work that case." This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/utah-authorities-connecting-serial-killer-152942415.html

articles.title: 3 Alexander brothers each get 30 years for sex trafficking after women speak in court
articles.summary: Real estate brokers Oren and Tal Alexander and their brother, Alon, listen as their lawyers argue for lesser sentences at a New York courtroom Tuesday. (Jane Rosenberg / Reuters) Two former luxury real estate brokers and their brother were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison, seven months after they were convicted of drugging and raping women in a sex trafficking ring. Federal prosecutors sought life sentences for Oren and Alon Alexander, a pair of former powerful real estate brokers, and their brother, Tal, in a New York City courtroom Tuesday afternoon. Attorneys for the brothers, who have asserted their innocence, asked the judge to give the men the mandatory minimum, instead. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni characterized the brothers as “Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.” On one side, they were described as gentlemen who loved their children, she said, and on the other, they were described as “sadistic, misogynistic, sexual predators.” “Your conduct was monstrous,” Caproni said in her sentencing. But Caproni added that she did not believe the Alexander brothers were beyond redemption, declining the request to give them life sentences. In addition to 30 years of incarceration, she ordered 10 years of supervised release and sex offender treatment approved by the probation office. They are not to have contact with any child under age 18 unless it is approved by the probation office. Twins Alon and Oren Alexander, 39, were ordered to pay $300,000 each in fines. Tal Alexander, 40, was ordered to pay $350,000. Caproni said she will ask the Bureau of Prisons to consult with experts about whether they should be allowed to be held together, as she believes they are bad influences on one another. The men were found guilty in March of 10 counts, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking and sex trafficking by force, after a trial that included testimony from 11 women who described being lured, drugged and sexually assaulted over a period of years. Six of the women were part of the indictment. Tal Alexander and Oren Alexander in New York in 2016. (Sean Zanni / Patrick McMullan via Getty file) In a sentencing memo, prosecutors in New York’s Southern District said more than 70 women came forward with allegations of abuse and accused the brothers of exploiting their wealth, influence and connections to target victims. Victim statements from 11 women, some using court-assigned pseudonyms, were read at the hearing before the judge’s decision. The women asked Caproni to impose a sentence that was appropriate for the profound impact the men had on their lives. One victim, Maya Miller, described the trauma of her rape by Tal Alexander as having settled into her nervous system. “I carry a quiet funeral inside me,” Miller said. Another victim, Olivia Lane, told the judge that she was “profoundly incapacitated” after having had a fraction of one drink while meeting Oren Alexander. She described being raped at least a dozen times while she was terrified and in pain. She then directly addressed the men. “You are weak. You are inhumane,” Lane said. “You never had power, and look at you now.” Two women described the men as having almost inhuman eyes during their assaults. Isa Brooks said, “Their eyes went black during the attack, like I was being mauled by animals.” Lane said, “I remember looking at him and seeing a monster, black eyes.” The women also emphasized the Alexander brothers’ lack of remorse or acknowledgment of their victims throughout the trial. Victim Katie Moore noted in her statement that after five weeks of trial and having been found guilty, the men “cannot even look us in the eye as we speak today.” “These men spent years treating women and girls like their humanity meant nothing,” Moore said. The brothers honed their methods together, attacking women in a way that was designed to humiliate and degrade them, prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said at the sentencing. “When they were done, they bragged to each other and their friends. ... The defendants knew exactly what they were doing, and they did it anyway, and they did it over and over and over again,” she said. Oren Alexander, 37, center, and his twin brother, Alon, center-right, speak to their attorney Joel Denaro during their bond hearing at the Richard E. Gerstein Justice Building on Dec. 13, 2024, in Miami. (Matias J. Ocner / Miami Herald via Getty file) At trial, prosecutors said the brothers raped the women after having promised them parties and trips. One woman testified that she lost control of her body after she had a drink with Alon Alexander at a New York City club. When she awoke, she testified, they were naked on a bed. She kept trying to get up, and he kept pushing her back down, she said. When she told him that she didn’t want to have sex with him, she testified, he responded, “‘You already did.’” In a sentencing submission, attorneys for the brothers acknowledged that they sometimes behaved insensitively toward women but categorically denied that any of them had raped or sexually assaulted anyone. At trial, the attorneys described the sex as consensual and said the women were motivated in part by financial gain. “All the stories were rehearsed,” Tal Alexander’s attorney, Deanna Paul, said in her closing argument. “They’re looking for money.” Paul urged the judge to consider giving her client the mandatory minimum of 15 years in prison, saying the verdict has not changed her view of the evidence. She said 15 years is already an extraordinary punishment, so “what would another 20 or 30 years accomplish?” Attorneys for the two other brothers similarly asked Caproni to give the men 15 years. Marc Agnifilo, who represents Oren Alexander, told her the men all stopped their “sexually aggressive” behavior after they met  their wives. “All three defendants stopped, and that matters,” Agnifilo said. Each of the brothers was given an opportunity to address the court directly before he was issued his sentence. Oren Alexander was the first to ask Caproni for a lighter sentence. He once again denied the assaults in his comments before he assaulted her that he has built a new life and family. “My son needs me, and I need to be there for him, and I ask your honor to impose the minimum sentence,” he said. Tal Alexander, who was next to speak, expressed regret over his past actions. “The person who stands in court is not the same man as before,” he said, asking Caproni to consider the entirety of his life in the decision. “I wish I showed more maturity,” he said. “I cannot undo moments when I was immature and careless with other people’s feelings. I understand the jury found me guilty, and I know words cannot change that.” The last brother to speak, Alon, insisted that he was innocent and that he had never raped any women. He invoked his two young daughters in asking for the mercy of the court. “I am afraid of being Daddy in the photograph,” he said. Caproni appeared unmoved by their statements, emphasizing that the rapes were not a result of “party culture or hookup culture” as they described. She said it was not enough to rape the women — the brothers sought to humiliate them, she asserted. “That marriage would transform them from sexual predators to normal gentlemen, I disagree,” Caproni said. “Rape is about power. ... Having a girlfriend or a wife doesn’t mean you are not going to rape or humiliate women.” This article was originally published on NBCNews.com This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/ex-luxury-real-estate-brokers-brother-sentenced-federal-sex-traffickin-rcna605818

articles.title: 美联储决议考验市场，美股盘前SK海力士涨约8%，希捷科技跌约4%，油价止跌
articles.summary: 美股盘前，SK海力士季度业绩大幅超预期，营业利润同比暴增七倍，叠加百万亿韩元史诗级股东回报计划，令人工智能相关板块情绪明显升温。与此同时，市场正屏息等待微软、Alphabet财报及美联储利率决议，多重重大事件风险集中于同一交易日。 SK海力士盘前涨幅约8%，其亮眼业绩重燃投资者对AI资本开支前景的信心，推动科技股资金轮动回流。标普500期货小幅走高，纳斯达克100指数有望实现三连涨。 然而，市场并非全线向好。恩智浦三季度营收增长19%虽超预期，但四季度指引低于市场预期，盘前跌约8%；希捷科技因季度业绩指引逊于分析师预期，盘前跌约4%，显示科技板块内部分化加剧。 美联储预计将在本次会议上维持利率不变，但主席沃什届时可能面临压力，需就当前暂停加息的理由作出解释——上个月美联储曾一致投票决定加息以应对通胀压力。 美股盘前，希捷科技跌约4%，公司季度业绩指引逊色于分析师预期。恩智浦跌约8%，公司Q3营收增19%超预期，但Q4指引低于预期。SK海力士涨约8%，公司三季度营业利润同比暴增7倍，祭出百万亿韩元史诗级股东回报。 欧洲斯托克50指数开盘涨0.2%，德国DAX指数跌0.2%，英国富时100指数跌0.3%，法国CAC 40指数涨0.3%。 日经225指数收涨1.1%，报63954.19点。日本东证指数收跌0.1%，报3991.71点。韩国首尔综指收涨6.6%，报6012.44点。SK海力士涨近11%，三星电子涨约9%。 美国10年期国债收益率上涨3个基点，至5.02% 日本10年期收益率上涨3个基点，至2.825% 现货黄金下跌0.7%，报每盎司4,029.94美元 布伦特原油结束两日连跌，上涨1.8%至每桶约115.90美元。 AI情绪回暖，科技股全线受提振 美股盘前，希捷科技下跌约4%，原因是公司季度业绩指引逊于分析师预期。恩智浦跌幅更深，约达8%——尽管该公司第三季度营收同比增长19%并超出预期，但第四季度指引不及市场预期，令投资者感到失望。 SK海力士的强劲业绩为近期承压的科技股注入了一剂强心针。JonesTrading Institutional Services LLC首席市场策略师Michael O'Rourke在报告中写道，"一波AI相关消息在该板块承压三周后引发了一轮情绪修复式反弹"，这些消息"让投资者相信，大型AI企业有能力、且正在持续推进资本支出，即便规模较小的企业仍面临压力"。 彭博市场策略师Mark Cranfield表示，押注AI驱动的反弹能够穿越美联储决议的投资者，将从SK海力士和三星电子引领亚洲市场走高中获得信心，"这令人回想起今年上半年，彼时对AI主题的热情似乎对油价上涨和债券收益率走高免疫"。 科技股本周的回升也受益于Anthropic提交S-1招股文件及多项融资计划等消息的共同催化。 美联储决议在即，利率路径存在不确定性 市场在为AI热情定价的同时，还需应对美联储政策方向带来的压力。美联储预计将在本次会议上维持利率不变，但主席Kevin Warsh届时可能面临压力，需就当前暂停加息的理由作出解释——上个月美联储曾一致投票决定加息以应对通胀压力。 美联储上月发布的预测显示，官员支持年内再加息一次。投资者周二对本次会议加息的概率定价不足10%，但已将年内最后一次政策会议即12月会议视为可能的加息时间窗口。 基准10年期美国国债收益率上升2个基点至5.02%。Westpac Banking Corp固定收益研究主管Damien McColough表示，"FOMC的措辞将继续保持鹰派，在通胀问题上保持警惕，加上市场可能重新聚焦油价走势，应会带来偏空的驱动力。" 油价止跌，地缘政治风险升温 油价方面，布伦特原油结束两日连跌，上涨1.8%至每桶约115.90美元。据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士报道，美国已告知多个海湾国家，需为中期选举后可能发生的一场短暂而激烈的伊朗军事冲突做好准备。 在货币市场，彭博美元强势指数连续第四日上涨，新西兰元兑澳元下跌近2%，创2017年以来最大单日跌幅，此前新西兰央行意外宣布维持利率不变。黄金下跌0.7%至每盎司约4030美元。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI液冷龙头Vertiv Q3营收同比增长61%，订单增度超100%，盘前暴涨超15% | 财报见闻
articles.summary: 作为数据中心电源与散热解决方案的关键供应商，Vertiv第三季度收入、利润、订单与现金流同步大幅加速，全年关键指标全面上调，盘前股价一度涨逾15%。 Vertiv第三季度净销售额达43.13亿美元，同比增长61%，较公司此前指引上限高出逾12%，调整后摊薄每股收益（EPS）达2.21美元，同比增长78%，较市场一致预期高出约21%。 公司披露第三季度有机订单同比增速超过100% ，这一数字改变了市场对增长持续性的判断——订单增速大幅高于收入增速，意味着当前的高景气度具备向未来延伸的基础。 公司随即将全年净销售额指引中值上调至146.5亿美元，较此前中值提高6.5亿美元； 全年调整后摊薄EPS指引中值上调至7.15美元，较此前提高约6.7%，亦较财报前市场一致预期高约6.2%。Vertiv首席执行官Giordano Albertazzi表示： "我们正处于有史以来规模最大的基础设施建设浪潮之中，且这一浪潮仍在加速。" 三季度收入、利润、现金流全线大幅加速 第三季度净销售额43.13亿美元，同比增长61.2%， 其中有机增长贡献55个百分点，并购贡献约6个百分点。增长具有明显的地域广度：美洲收入增长74.5%（有机增长66.2%），亚太增长49.9%（有机增长48.3%），欧洲、中东及非洲地区（EMEA）增长22.8%（有机增长19.3%）。 盈利能力方面， 调整后营业利润达10.87亿美元，同比增长82.5%；调整后营业利润率为25.2%，同比提升290个基点，超出公司原指引上限（25%）20个基点。 GAAP营业利润率为22.8%，同比提升350个基点。Albertazzi将利润率改善归因于规模效应与制造效率提升，部分被产品组合变化和持续增长投入所抵消。 现金流方面，第三季度经营现金流为7.94亿美元，同比增长64%；调整后自由现金流为6.52亿美元，同比增长50%。截至9月底，公司流动性升至62亿美元，维持净现金头寸。 超预期幅度异常：远超普通"财报Beat" 此次超预期幅度不寻常。在收入规模已超40亿美元的体量下，实际收入较市场一致预期约37.6亿美元高出约15%，较公司原指引上限高出约4.63亿美元，绝对金额差异显著。调整后摊薄EPS为2.21美元，市场预期约为1.82美元，超出约21%。 更关键的是，此次超预期并非依赖费用压缩或税率变化，而是收入、有机增长、营业利润率与EPS同步显著优于预期，反映的是产能释放、项目交付提速与经营杠杆的共振。值得对比的是，二季度收入同比增长24.1%但略低于一致预期，彼时管理层将部分原因归结为项目执行时点偏移；三季度的强劲兑现，为这一解释提供了有力背书，修复了市场对项目交付能力的折价评估。 有机订单同比增速翻倍 公司披露第三季度有机订单同比增速超过100%。 这是本次财报最具长期定价意义的数据点。收入反映过去订单的兑现，而订单增速决定未来收入走势。订单增速大幅高于55%的有机收入增速，意味着积压订单仍在持续扩大，市场得以更有依据地将当前高增长向未来延伸，而非将三季度视为一次性交付高峰。 执行主席Dave Cote表示： "行业技术变化越快，对我们越有利。我们持续投入，持续建设，我们所建立的一切都是为了规模化而设计的。" 需要指出的是，公司未在财报附件中披露最新的订单积压总量或订单出货比，订单转化为收入仍需经历排产、交付与验收环节，存在一定的时序不确定性。 全面上调全年及四季度指引，但上调动能主要来自三季度已兑现部分 在全年指引层面，公司将净销售额指引区间上调至144.5亿—148.5亿美元，中值146.5亿美元；有机收入增长指引由此前约31%提升至38%；调整后摊薄EPS指引区间为7.10—7.20美元，中值7.15美元，同比增长约70%；调整后自由现金流指引提升至26亿—28亿美元。 四季度方面，公司指引净销售额为43.13亿—45.13亿美元，有机收入增长49%—51%，调整后摊薄EPS为2.22—2.28美元，同比增长约65%，中值约2.25美元，较财报前市场一致预期约2.21美元高出约1.8%。 需要注意的是，全年收入指引中值上调约6.5亿美元，而三季度实际收入已较原指引中值高出约5.63亿美元；全年EPS中值上调0.45美元，三季度实际EPS已较原指引中值高出约0.41美元。换言之，全年指引上调的绝大部分来自三季度已经兑现的超预期，四季度新增上调幅度相对有限。 区域与产品结构：美洲主导，EMEA出现边际修复 分区域来看，美洲贡献了约78%的季度收入增量，绝对主导本季增长；亚太近50%的有机增长与EMEA约20%的有机增长共同扩展了增长的地理基础。 从调整后营业利润率看，EMEA本季度为28.0%，同比提升920个基点，改善幅度最为突出；亚太为17.0%，同比提升380个基点；美洲为29.4%，同比基本持平。值得关注的是，EMEA前三季度累计有机收入仍同比下降3.3%，但三季度已恢复增长，利润率显著改善，尽管持续性仍有待后续季度验证。 分产品与服务来看，产品收入有机增长约63.6%，服务及备件有机增长约18.1%，服务的高报表增速中包含较多并购贡献，真实内生增长明显低于产品端。随着装机规模扩大，服务与生命周期管理能否逐步提速，将影响未来收入的稳定性。 经营现金流强劲，但递延收入贡献不可忽视 前三季度经营现金流达26.61亿美元，同比增长约140%；调整后自由现金流为22.30亿美元，同比增长约128%，表面现金转化率较高。但需要注意的是，前三季度递延收入增加约23.13亿美元，是经营现金流的重要支撑。 资产负债表显示，与2025年底相比，存货从14.57亿美元升至32.88亿美元，增长约126%，显著高于收入增速；递延收入从18.15亿美元增至41.21亿美元，增长约127%。存货快速积累反映公司处于主动扩产备货阶段，而递延收入的大幅增加则来自客户提前预付款，在一定程度上反映需求可见性较高，同时也意味着当前现金流中有部分尚待交付兑现。 公司维持全年资本开支约占收入4%的预期，三季度资本开支及资本化软件投入合计约1.42亿美元，较上年同期约增两倍，显示公司仍处于明显的产能扩张投入期。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “避险不再安全，仿佛回到1999年”，美银：美股防御板块泡沫已悄然超越科技股
articles.summary: 当市场将医疗和消费必需品视为AI交易的避风港时，这些"安全资产"本身已悄然演变为新的泡沫。美国银行最新研究显示，美股防御性板块的泡沫风险读数已超越科技股、纳斯达克乃至比特币，这一现象与1999年互联网泡沫顶峰时期的市场结构高度吻合。 美银衍生品团队在最新一期《全球股票波动率洞察》报告中指出，随着AI交易出现动摇，资金涌入医疗和消费必需品板块的"避险轮动"已将这两个板块的泡沫风险指标（BRI）推至历史高位。截至10月23日，美国医疗板块BRI读数约为0.8，为美银追踪的所有资产中最高，消费必需品约为0.74，能源约为0.7；相比之下，科技板块仅约0.5，纳斯达克约0.3，"七巨头"仅约0.25。 这一格局意味着，原本用于对冲AI风险的"防御性"资产，其价格泡沫化程度已显著高于其所对冲的标的本身。与此同时，美银全球金融压力指数上周从+0.09升至+0.20，创4月以来最高水平，市场整体压力环境正在趋于恶化。 防御性板块BRI超越科技股，历史先例指向互联网泡沫顶峰 美银的BRI是一个纯粹基于价格的指标，综合资产的回报率、波动率、动量及"脆弱性"，生成0至1之间的单一泡沫读数，0.8以上被标记为泡沫风险偏高。该指标曾于今年6月率先标记纳斯达克越过"泡沫阈值"。 美银本周新增了一张覆盖30年的BRI热力图，追踪标普500各板块的历史读数。数据显示，在1990年代末互联网狂热期间，以及2020年后的新冠疫情行情中，泡沫读数几乎在所有板块同步走高，防御性板块亦不例外。 美银据此得出结论：在结构性泡沫市场中，即便基本面并不支撑，各板块均可能出现泡沫化动态。换言之，当整个市场进入反身性循环，连牙膏和制药公司也会开始像动量股一样交易。美银认为，医疗和消费必需品板块出现泡沫迹象，进一步印证了其此前的判断——市场正迈向"日益反身性、易于暴涨暴跌的机制"。 泡沫仍属局部，与2000年顶峰尚有差距 尽管信号令人警惕，美银同时强调，当前泡沫的扩散程度远不及2000年。目前标普500中BRI超过0.8的个股约为15只，而互联网泡沫最疯狂时期这一数字为50至100只。 从市值权重来看，差距更为悬殊：当前这15只个股合计仅占标普500市值的约2.2%，而互联网泡沫顶峰时期这一比例高达20%至40%。 这15只个股的构成颇为耐人寻味，足以令任何1999年的日内交易者感到困惑：Moderna（MRNA）、Zebra（ZBRA）、CrowdStrike（CRWD）、IFF和Revvity（RVTY）位居前列，可口可乐（KO）、Amgen（AMGN）、Cboe（CBOE）和Palo Alto（PANW）紧随其后。可口可乐出现在泡沫股名单上，本身即是当前市场异象的最佳注脚。 泡沫蔓延至高股息与低波动主题，金融压力指数升至4月高位 美银已将BRI扩展至热门股票主题的追踪。在各主题中，云计算的泡沫读数最高（尽管尚未达到极端水平），其次是油气和高股息。单周涨幅最大的则是高股息股票，其次是低波动率股票和生物科技——这意味着泡沫正在蔓延至那些"让你安心等待收益"的资产类别。 在美银自定义篮子中，泡沫热点更为分散：巴西大选篮子BRI读数高达0.94，美国网络安全篮子为0.92，美国软件为0.76，油气（不含可再生能源）为0.73，制药超大规模算力为0.70，日本防御性股票同为0.70。读数接近于零的则是中国互联网、澳门博彩及中国反内卷篮子。 与此同时，美银全球金融压力指数升至+0.20，为4月以来最高，大宗商品和股票是压力最集中的资产类别，原油隐含波动率压力升至7月31日以来最高，欧洲压力指数亦已超过长期中位数。美银的GFSI风险配置器已从前一周的中性转为低配4.9%。 美银建议非对称保护，而非直接减仓 articles.title: 复刻SpaceX认购热？Anthropic IPO拟向散户开放最高20%份额，摩根大通主导揽客、戴蒙或亲自参与
articles.summary: Anthropic即将登陆资本市场，这场潜在的史上最大规模科技IPO正在向散户投资者敞开大门。 彭博援引知情人士报道， Anthropic已选定摩根大通主导其IPO美国散户部分的股份销售，花旗集团则负责协调国际散户发行。摩根大通首席执行官Jamie Dimon（杰米·戴蒙）预计将亲自参与该行的揽客活动。 据彭博报道，投资者向承销商反映，他们对Anthropic的合理估值已上调至约1.4万亿至1.5万亿美元，而1.75万亿美元的估值亦存在实现可能。 此次散户安排直接复刻了摩根大通此前在SpaceX IPO中的角色——SpaceX估值862亿美元的IPO吸引了逾1000亿美元的散户需求，创下历史纪录。Anthropic此番能否再度引爆散户热情，市场高度关注。 散户份额最高占比两成，摩根大通全面铺开渠道 报道称，Anthropic正在考虑将IPO总发行量的约15%至20%划拨给散户投资者。摩根大通的揽客范围涵盖高净值客户、私人银行客户及经纪商平台，覆盖面广泛。 花旗集团负责协调国际散户发行，Anthropic的IPO招股文件显示，国际发行涉及澳大利亚、加拿大、日本、欧洲经济区部分国家、瑞士及英国。 相关磋商仍在进行中，包括散户份额比例在内的具体细节均可能发生变化。Anthropic、摩根大通及花旗集团的代表均拒绝置评。 高盛、摩根士丹利主承销 Anthropic已于本周一正式向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交IPO申请，此次上市将由公司及部分现有投资者共同出售股份，高盛和摩根士丹利担任主承销商。 这是首家以开发顶尖AI模型为核心业务的公司寻求上市，Claude背后的财务状况也因此首次向公众披露——外界不仅得以了解其盈利规模，亦可窥见其潜在亏损情况。 AI军备竞赛烧钱不止，巨头竞相融资千亿 Anthropic此次IPO的背后，是整个AI行业对资金的巨大渴求。AI模型开发及相关基础设施建设所需的资金规模，已促使各大公司动辄一次性融资数百亿美元。 Meta Platforms本周一启动了一项最高融资980亿美元的股权计划，若成功落地，将成为史上规模最大的同类融资之一；此前，谷歌母公司Alphabet已于今年早些时候完成850亿美元的股权融资计划。 与此同时，Anthropic与竞争对手OpenAI在寻求创纪录融资的过程中，也面临日益严峻的公众审视——一系列由"流氓代理"（rogue agents）发起的高知名度黑客事件，令AI安全问题持续引发外界关切。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 单季净利率1.45%，乖宝宠物仍选择不打价格战
articles.summary: 10 月 27 日晚间，乖宝宠物（ 301498.SZ ）披露未经审计的 2026 年第三季度报告。前三季度公司实现营业收入 51.25 亿元，同比增长 8.17%；归母净利润 2.14 亿元，同比下降 58.35%；扣非净利润 2.14 亿元，同比下降 56.50%。第三季度单季营业收入 15.82 亿元，同比增长 4.27%；归母净利润 2300.63 万元，同比下降 82.96%；扣非净利润 2389.38 万元，同比下降 80.93%。 单季降幅比累计降幅高出 24.6 个百分点，利润的压力集中在第三季度。按公告数据计算，第三季度单季净利率 1.45%，上年同期约 8.9%。 公司在三季报针对主要会计数据变动原因给出的解释是汇率波动、原材料上涨导致毛利率下降，加之境内自有品牌及直销占比提升、相应费率上升。前三季度营业成本 31.17 亿元，对应毛利率 39.18%，较上年同期的 42.83% 下降 3.65 个百分点。 费用端的压力更直接。前三季度销售费用 12.41 亿元、同比增加 2.07 亿元，管理费用 3.27 亿元、增加 0.58 亿元，财务费用由上年同期的 -0.11 亿元转为 0.51 亿元，这三项合计多支出 3.27 亿元；同期营业利润 3.14 亿元、同比减少 3.58 亿元。研发费用 0.68 亿元、同比下降 3.7%，是主要费用项中唯一减少的一项。销售费用率由 21.82% 升至 24.22%，而收入增速只有 8.17%。 财务费用的跳升主要来自汇兑。汇兑损益及手续费等约 5145 万元，这一影响同时落在权益端，前三季度外币财务报表折算差额为 -5639.28 万元，上年同期为 +584.36 万元。 乖宝宠物第三季度境内自有品牌收入与去年同期基本持平，增速较上半年出现阶段性回调。接近人士透露原因有两个，一是弗列加特 7、8 月受到舆情影响，二是主动优化麦富迪、霸弗等品牌的产品、渠道及费用结构；公司更关注增长质量和可持续性，不以单一季度的规模表现作为主要经营目标。 乖宝宠物今年不赌单季爆发，重心放在价格体系、老客运营和投入产出效率上。公司定了三条纪律：不以大幅折扣换规模，必要时宁可断货；预算按投放效果动态调整；增长、老客与盈利三者兼顾。单季净利率已降至 1.45%，它选择守价格、守费用，不守规模。 利润表之外的信号集中在现金流与负债。前三季度经营活动现金流净额 5302.59 万元、同比下降 89.35%，净现比约 24.8%；购买商品、接受劳务支付的现金 32.66 亿元、同比增长 17.4%，快于收入增速。在建工程 4.81 亿元、较年初增长 717.20%，无形资产 4.17 亿元、增长 157.44%（主要系购入 NPFG 品牌资产）；短期借款 12.50 亿元、增长 315.30%，资产负债率由 20.45% 升至 35.49%，货币资金 13.13 亿元、增长 60.22%（主要系现金管理产品赎回）。 四季度不冲量，费用率就少了一条靠规模摊薄的路。销售费用增速比收入快 11.87 个百分点，而费用这一头公司明确要收紧，缺口只能靠收入补。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 1300亿美元财富一日蒸发，预测市场80%胜率翻车，巴西大选为美国中期选举敲响警钟
articles.summary: 预测市场在巴西大选中遭遇重大失准，引发了市场对这一新兴工具可靠性的深刻质疑。 巴西总统大选决选于10月25日落幕，现任左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西乌·卢拉·达席尔瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva）出人意料地击败保守派候选人Flávio Bolsonaro。 在投票日之前，Polymarket和Kalshi两大预测市场均将Bolsonaro的胜选概率标定在约80%。 巴西雷亚尔与基准股指Ibovespa在选前一路走高，反映出市场对Bolsonaro胜选的强烈预期。然而随着卢拉胜选消息传出，市场随即大幅逆转，做多投资者蒙受了沉重损失。 这一事件所引发的影响远不止于巴西本身。区区约3200万美元的Polymarket合约成交量，在选前数周内催生了约1300亿美元的股市财富，而这些财富在市场重新开盘后随即灰飞烟灭。彭博专栏作家Jonathan Levin指出， 此次事件更值得警惕的教训，在于传统投资者轻信预测市场赔率、将其直接用于金融资产定价的做法，而这一风险在即将到来的美国中期选举前夕尤为突出。 预测市场的先天缺陷 预测市场允许用户就现实世界事件的结果相互对赌，近一年来已饱受争议。据报道，美国司法部曾指控一名美国士兵利用有关突袭捕获时任委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗的机密信息，在Polymarket上下注获利；检察官亦指控Alphabet Inc.一名软件工程师利用内部数据，在谷歌"年度搜索"结果上进行押注。批评人士还担忧，预测市场带有成瘾性赌博属性，并可能在体育和政治领域制造腐败诱因，同时形成危险的反馈循环——赌盘赔率左右传统媒体和社交媒体的内容基调，进而影响公众认知乃至民主选举结果。 支持者则认为，预测市场在一定程度上能够汇聚群体智慧，为风险管理和公众决策提供参考，并模拟出过去只有对冲基金、保险公司等机构才能获取的预测模型输出。然而当合约规模较小、流动性不足时，预测市场所传递的信号可能误导多于启发，且市场的信息质量完全取决于参与者的认知水平。 三重警示：流动性、参与者与信息质量 此次巴西事件中，上述隐患早已有迹可循。巴西大选的Polymarket合约总成交量约为2.49亿美元，与2024年美国总统大选37亿美元的规模相去甚远，Kalshi市场的体量则更小。 更关键的是，在10月4日第一轮投票至10月25日决选期间，Bolsonaro的胜选概率从约64%跳升至80%，但这一阶段Polymarket的成交量不足3200万美元。其中大量交易集中在第一轮投票前后，以及决选日尾盘——彼时最高法院大法官Cristiano Zanin单方面宣布将投票时间延长两小时，引发市场剧烈波动。值得注意的是，Zanin曾担任卢拉的私人律师。 参与者结构同样存在严重问题。巴西财政部于今年4月封锁了Polymarket和Kalshi的访问权限，政府9月又颁布了更广泛的网络赌博禁令。这意味着，在决选关键窗口期内推动赔率变动的，几乎全为非巴西本地用户，其中不乏来自美国的加密货币圈人士。据报道，埃隆·马斯克于9月20日转发了一篇已删除的X平台帖子，内容涉及Polymarket赔率看好Bolsonaro，或进一步助推了相关资金流入。马斯克长期以来对Bolsonaro家族及拉丁美洲右翼势力持支持立场。 民调早有预警，市场视而不见 与预测市场的高置信度形成鲜明对比的是，传统民调从未显示出如此悬殊的差距。BTG Pactual/Nexus在决选前一天发布的民调显示，Bolsonaro支持率为50.5%，卢拉为49.5%，差距在2个百分点的误差范围之内。Datafolha于10月22日公布的调查则显示两人支持率完全持平。 尽管巴西观察人士习惯于预期Bolsonaro家族的实际得票会高于民调，但从上述数据到80%的胜选概率，这一逻辑跳跃难以自圆其说。Jonathan Levin指出，令人惊讶的并非预测市场本身出现误差，而是众多投资者在明显的预警信号面前，仍将这一赔率直接转化为金融资产的定价依据。 对美国中期选举的警示 巴西事件对即将举行的美国中期选举具有直接的借鉴意义，但两者之间也存在重要差异—— 最关键的一点在于，美国市场有大量真实选民参与。 即便如此，投资者和选民仍需汲取以下教训：其一，中期选举的预测市场交易活跃度通常远低于总统大选，许多具体选区合约的流动性远不及巴西大选；其二，不应将任何结果视为板上钉钉——这种先入之见或许正是让部分Bolsonaro支持者在决选日选择放弃投票、最终帮助卢拉翻盘的原因之一；其三，若要参考预测市场赔率，必须对相关市场的质量和参与者结构进行独立评估。 当预测市场与传统金融市场相互叠加时，误判的代价将被成倍放大。巴西的案例已然清晰地呈现了这一风险的量级。若同样的情形在美国中期选举中重演，其冲击将远不止于此。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美联储10月鹰派暂停：市场的交易预期差在哪里？
articles.summary: 北京时间29日凌晨，美联储将公布10月份利率决议。目前，OIS市场定价美联储10月加息概率已降至10%左右，但对12月加息的定价约75%。此前由9月份CPI数据超预期引发的10月加息押注，受到沃什及其他美联储官员近期表态的压制。 多位票委强调无需连续会议收紧政策，并保留根据后续数据调整政策的空间。在美联储关键官员密集表态以及中期选举前夕这一敏感时间节点下，市场已基本消化本次会议按兵不动的基准预期。本次FOMC会议的焦点由此将转向沃什对12月加息的态度、其对政策反应函数的解释，以及五个货币政策改革工作组是否披露具体进展。 尽管9月CPI显示通胀压力依然顽固，核心CPI环比上涨0.33%，且能源冲击已开始向航运、柴油及核心商品等下游环节传导，美国或已出现核心通胀扩散迹象；但与此同时，美债长端利率仍接近5%，较高融资成本持续压制房地产、企业投资与科技资产估值，AI板块也在资本开支可持续性、供应约束和融资风险等担忧下持续调整。在此背景下，市场关注点正从通胀担忧转向经济增长与金融条件收紧的风险。 本次FOMC最可能鹰派暂停，Hammack、Logan等官员或投下鹰派异议票，票型可能呈现9:3的分歧格局；同时，FOMC将通过声明措辞、投票分歧和记者会释放鹰派信号，以保留12月加息选项。 加之近期沃什在IMF年会期间拒绝就货币政策或美国经济前景发表评论，仅重申价格稳定承诺，这进一步加剧了沟通混乱。 因此，10月按兵不动真正的交易预期差在于：市场是否低估了鹰派暂停与12月加息的连续性；以及AI资本开支的供应成本担忧、中期选举和金融条件收紧这三大清算事件，可能在未来数周放大市场波动，并影响12月后的政策转向。 预期差的定价：12月才是风险锚

articles.title: 国内生猪价跌破9元/公斤，周期反转还会来吗？
articles.summary: 10月以来，生猪市场延续旺季不旺态势，国内生猪价格继续下行。截至10月27日，全国外三元生猪均价降至9.19元/公斤，较10月10日的10.11元/公斤下跌超过9%，部分省份如山西、湖南、四川等价格已跌破9元/公斤。 期货市场同步承压，生猪主力LH2701合约一度跌至9550元/吨附近，近远月合约普遍走弱。针对期价剧烈波动，大连商品交易所出台监管举措：自10月29日交易时起，将LH2701合约非期货公司会员或客户单日开仓量限制为500手，并同步上调该合约交易保证金至16%。监管收紧短期或放大市场波动，但有助于抑制过度投机与挤仓行为，引导资金理性交易，促使盘面回归供需与估值。 而与短期价格弱势形成鲜明对比，生猪中长期产能去化明显提速，供给收缩信号增强。Q3末，全国能繁母猪存栏量已降至3602万头，同比大幅下降10.7%，单季度环比降幅扩大至4.7%，较去年的高点累计去化超460万头。当前能繁母猪绝对数量已回落至农业部设定的3750万头正常保有量的96%左右，处于绿色调控区间中下部。 不过，产能下降尚未转化为商品猪供给的同步收缩。前三季度全国生猪出栏约5.37亿头，同比增长1.4%，出栏均重仍处高位。加上库存绝对水平仍高，供给收缩向商品猪出栏传导仍有时滞。 当前生猪市场呈“弱现实、强预期”格局。弱现实表现为，现货跌破现金流成本线，行业亏损逾8个月，冻品库存高企、出栏均重居高不下，终端消费疲软；生产效率提升与体重增加对冲母猪去化，供给收缩传导仍有时滞，供需宽松短期难改。但深度亏损正加大现金流压力，为产能出清创造条件。
